title: Enforce explicit resident-session history metadata at the client boundary
outcome: Consolidated tm-7p9z.7 dual review on fingerprint aa6562ad4be15ca3909715c5cc0517eb71292d2b64974f13b4e8b0b55ebc30af: Codex found no defect; Claude identified a type-enforcement gap after resolveHasOlderSessionHistory began trusting only explicit hasOlderHistory. Every inspected current normalizer supplies the flags, so this is preventive type hardening, not a reproduced paging regression or P1 bug. ui/src/types.ts:408 currently makes hasOlderHistory/hasNewerHistory optional. IMPORTANT: Rust Session in src/wire.rs does not serialize these client-only window fields, and the TypeScript Session type is reused for raw targeted responses. Introduce a clear normalized resident-session contract (or equivalent constructor/producer invariant) requiring both booleans after admission, while keeping the raw wire shape honest. Preserve no-inference pagination, FOLLOW/STAY and stale-response ordering. Related tm-jzce already fixes complete-window overlap flag values; it does not cover this type-boundary gap and must not be reopened as the same defect.
acceptance: Normalized resident sessions require explicit older/newer history booleans; raw API responses are not falsely typed as containing client-only fields. Summary materialization, targeted hydration, history merges and reconciliation produce the required shape with focused coverage. Missing untrusted fields do not restore count/messagesLoaded fallback paging. TypeScript and current history/navigation regression tests pass without changing scroll gestures or stale-response admission.
